# Gengchou v2.5.0

v2.5.0 adds Grok as a fourth quota provider and fixes a credential probe that
silently never worked inside WSL for any provider. The executable, settings,
cache, and update identities are unchanged.

## Changes

- Add **Grok** alongside Claude, Codex, and Antigravity. Gengchou reads the
  session that `grok login` already stored and asks the same billing endpoint
  the CLI's own `/usage` view uses, so the percentage and reset time come from
  xAI rather than from any local estimate. The window length is measured from
  the reported billing period instead of assumed from its type, so a calendar
  month shows its real 28-31 days.
- `~/.grok/auth.json` can hold sign-ins from several identity providers.
  Only an entry issued by xAI itself is used, and its token is only ever sent
  to xAI. An `XAI_API_KEY` environment variable is a fallback for the CLI, not
  a session, and is not read.
- Fix WSL credential probes for **every** provider. Gengchou asked
  `wsl.exe` to run its probe script with `--`, which hands the arguments to the
  distribution's login shell as one command line; the shell re-parsed them,
  dropped the quoting, and ran the script statement by statement, so the path
  each script computes was empty by the time it was used. A credential that
  existed only inside WSL was therefore reported as absent. Claude, Codex,
  Antigravity, and Grok are all fixed by this change.
- Persist Grok in the usage cache, so its value is shown immediately after a
  restart instead of waiting for the first poll like every other provider.
- Stop rejecting an entire settings file because it names a provider this build
  does not know. The unknown entry is dropped and every other setting is kept.

## Updating

Settings migrate automatically. An existing installation keeps the answer it
already gave to the one-time credential prompt, so Grok is not asked about
again; it is also not switched on by itself. When a Grok session is detected,
Gengchou raises a single notification, and Grok appears only after you enable
it under **Providers**.

Downgrading to v2.4.2 or earlier after running this release resets your
settings. Those versions cannot read a provider list that names Grok, fall back
to defaults, and overwrite the stored layout, language, and provider selection.
This release and later ones ignore provider names they do not recognize, so the
same downgrade is safe from here on.

Do not update an installation older than v2.2.4 directly to this release. The
v2.2.4 release remains available as the required bridge.
